passage.author: Henry David Thoreau
passage.text: The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation. What is called resignation is confirmed desperation.

links.reason: You both describe holding it together on the outside while something heavier sits underneath.

passage.author: Mary Shelley
passage.text: I am alone and miserable; man will not associate with me; but one as deformed and horrible as myself would not deny herself to me.

links.reason: You both name the ache of being surrounded by people and still having no one who is yours.

passage.author: Charles Dickens
passage.text: Heaven knows we need never be ashamed of our tears, for they are rain upon the blinding dust of earth, overlying our hard hearts.

links.reason: You both describe missing a place while being relieved to be gone.
